title: Argon2 password verification needs resource bounds under login/step-up bursts

original_titles.title: Argon2id hashing not explicitly bounded by a semaphore/thread pool

problem: Argon2id is configured with memory/time cost, but the API does not show an explicit bounded semaphore or dedicated worker pool limiting concurrent hash/verify operations. A burst of concurrent login/step-up attempts can multiply CPU and memory use.
impact: Attackers may use authentication endpoints to exhaust memory/CPU even when rate limits exist, especially across multiple API workers.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Measure Argon2 memory/latency on the production VM and calculate safe maximum concurrent verifications.
Add a bounded semaphore or dedicated executor per process for hash/verify operations; reject or queue excess requests with 429/503 and Retry-After.
Combine this with distributed per-IP/per-account rate limits so multiple workers cannot multiply the allowed concurrency arbitrarily.
Add load tests measuring memory peak, p95 login latency and rejection under credential-stuffing bursts.

acceptance_criteria: Authentication burst cannot exceed the measured memory budget.
Excessive attempts are throttled with a documented retry response.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
